name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican nominee outraised Democrat by roughly 100-to-1 with outside support
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95%
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but does not change the partisan baseline
model.rationale: The R+13 lean, Steinmann's dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing the Republican near 95% all point the same direction, with no polls or headlines suggesting a competitive race. The forecast stays at a roughly 15-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major Republican primary fallout, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Houston-area seat is a strongly Republican district, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward the GOP. Morgan Luttrell is retiring, so the Republican nominee, Jessica Hart Steinmann, runs to hold the seat against Democrat Laura Jones.

The money gap is enormous: Steinmann has raised over $2 million and drawn outside support, while Jones has raised about $22,000. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 95%. With no polls and no expert ratings flagging the race, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
